body.x: Individual Consultant – Strengthening Development Bank of Solomon Islands (DBSI) Institutional Readiness for GCF Accreditation – Environmental & Social Safeguards

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page.
Application Deadline: Shown in the bottom of the page. All applications must be submitted by 10:00 PM (KST) on the closing date.

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) was established as an intergovernmental organization with the objective of promoting sustainable development of developing and emerging countries, including the least developed countries. GGGI is dedicated to supporting the creation and diffusion of the model of economic growth known as “green growth”, which integrates economic growth, environmental sustainability, poverty reduction, and social inclusion. GGGI supports governments to strengthen climate finance access, institutional capacity and sustainable investment.

Pacific Island Countries (PICs), though modest in terrestrial extent, encompass vast maritime jurisdictions and exhibit profound geographic, economic, ecological, and cultural diversity. These nations remain disproportionately vulnerable to the adverse impacts of climate change—including intensified tropical cyclones, sea-level rise, prolonged droughts, and rising ambient temperatures—which collectively undermine economic stability, erode human and physical capital, and impede long-term, climate-resilient development pathways. Consequently, there is an urgent imperative to accelerate access to climate finance for Small Island Developing States (SIDS), ensure efficient mobilization of resources, and expedite their translation into actionable, high-impact projects. Notwithstanding notable progress in project approval processes, the current scale and velocity of financial disbursements to the region remain insufficient relative to the existential climate threats confronting Pacific nations.

A principal constraint to the effective access, absorption, and deployment of climate finance lies in institutional capacity gaps within key national entities—including line ministries, national financing mechanisms, regionally and nationally designated accredited entities, and development banks. Such limitations frequently result in significant implementation delays, even following the approval of funding. Furthermore, lessons derived from completed climate interventions are often neither systematically documented nor disseminated to inform the design and execution of subsequent initiatives. In light of the enhanced mandates for accelerated climate finance delivery emerging from the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31), a substantial increase in financial flows to SIDS is anticipated in the near term. It is therefore imperative that PICs proactively strengthen their institutional readiness to capitalize on this opportunity. The forthcoming five-year period represents a critical window for unlocking sustainable finance mechanisms in the Pacific and reinforcing national capacities for effective absorption and implementation, thereby enabling meaningful progress toward climate resilience and sustainable development objectives prior to 2030.

The Green Climate Fund (GCF), established under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), constitutes the world's largest dedicated financial mechanism for climate action. As a global investment platform, the GCF catalyses a paradigm shift toward low-emission and climate-resilient development pathways. Operating through a country-owned partnership model, the Fund serves as the long-term financial instrument mandated to deliver an ambitious and scaled contribution to the achievement of international climate objectives under the Paris Agreement.

The DBSI has been nominated by the National Designated Authority (NDA)/ Focal Point as one of the national entities seeking accreditation to GCF. At the outset, a DBSI GCF accreditation gap assessment was undertaken in 2023 under the SPREP-facilitated Readiness Support. Existing and planned SPREP support remains important; this targeted GGGI assignment is intended to complement it without duplicating activities or financing. DBSI will provide evidence of measures undertaken since the assessment for a concise cross-check, rather than a new comprehensive assessment.

GGGI, in collaboration with the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change, Disaster Management and Meteorology (MECDM), in its capacity as the GCF NDA is supporting DBSI to strengthen its Environmental and Social Safeguards (ESS) Policy/Framework. This technical assistance aims to enhance DBSI’s institutional readiness for GCF accreditation pre-screening and the subsequent submission of an accreditation application, ideally within the first half of 2027, subject to institutional readiness and applicable GCF procedures.

GGGI is therefore seeking a short-term individual consultant to develop clear, proportionate and usable DBSI ESS documents aligned with applicable GCF ESS requirements and the Revised Accreditation Framework (RAF), as well as relevant SIG laws and policies. The work will include consultation with MECDM’s Environment and Conservation Division (ECD), which is responsible for administering the Environment Act 1998, the Environment Regulations 2008 and other applicable national environmental laws and policies.

This consultancy aims to develop a Board-ready ESS Policy/Framework and supporting operational tools for DBSI that meet applicable GCF ESS and accreditation requirements while remaining proportionate to the Solomon Islands context and DBSI’s current capacity. The Consultant will undertake the following focused activities within the defined budget and timeline:
Deliverable 1 – Initial Draft and Targeted Review
Hold inception meeting with DBSI, the NDA/MECDM and GGGI to agree focal points, document access and the consultation plan.
Review the 2023 gap assessment and available DBSI evidence at a targeted level, recording remaining document gaps without repeating the full assessment.
Prepare initial drafts of the ESS Policy/Framework, drawing on existing DBSI practices and applicable standards.
Consult DBSI and MECDM (NDA and ECD) on national requirements, including the Environment Act 1998 and Environment Regulations 2008, as well as relevant social safeguards stakeholders.

Develop practical ESS screening, risk categorization, due diligence, mitigation and management, grievance handling, monitoring and reporting procedures and templates appropriate to DBSI’s financing operations.
Keep responsibilities and procedures proportionate to DBSI’s current capacity, identifying longer-term improvements separately.
Facilitate focused validation consultations with DBSI, MECDM, GGGI and relevant government counterparts.
Submit the final, editable, Board-ready ESS Policy/Framework, supporting operational templates and a phased implementation note.
Deliver one practical orientation session for DBSI personnel on ESS screening and application of the framework.
The following deliverables will be expected to be delivered by the consultant.

Deliverable 1: Inception Report and Initial Draft ESS Policy/Framework Methodology, work plan and consultation plan Agreed focal points and document access Initial draft ESS Policy/Framework Short document inventory and outstanding gaps list | 1 month after contract signing | 20%

Deliverable 2: Updated ESS Policy/Framework, Operational Tools and Consultation Summary Updated draft ESS Policy/Framework package Operational screening and risk-management tools (screening, risk categorization, due diligence, mitigation, grievance, monitoring and reporting) Consultation summary (DBSI, NDA/MECDM, ECD and social safeguards stakeholders) | 1.5 months after contract signing | 35%

Deliverable 3: Final Board-ready ESS Policy/Framework and Tools Final editable, Board-ready ESS Policy/Framework Supporting operational templates and tools Phased implementation note Validation summary Staff orientation materials | 2 months after contract signing | 45%

The consultancy is expected to require an estimated 40 workdays over a total duration of two (2) months from contract signing. The milestone dates above are indicative and will be reconfirmed against the actual contracting date.

The Consultant will report to the designated GGGI project lead and coordinate closely with DBSI and the NDA/MECDM, including MECDM’s Environment and Conservation Division (ECD) on national environmental requirements. DBSI remains responsible for the formal institutional and Board approval of the ESS Policy/Framework.
All deliverables must be submitted in English, in both editable format (e.g., Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and PDF format, unless otherwise specified.
Reports must adhere to GGGI’s standard formatting guidelines (to be provided upon contract signing) and maintain a high standard of professional quality, clarity, and conciseness.
All data, analyses, and models developed must be clearly documented and transferred to GGGI upon completion.
The DBSI Environmental & Social Safeguards Consultant will require the following qualifications, experience, competencies and language skills:
Advanced degree in environmental management, social sciences, development finance, public policy, law or a related discipline.
At least five (5) years of relevant policy, environmental and social safeguards, and institutional risk-management experience.
Demonstrated experience developing ESS procedures for financial institutions.

Knowledge of GCF ESS and accreditation requirements, including the Revised Accreditation Framework; Pacific and Solomon Islands experience, including familiarity with Solomon Islands environmental legislation, is desirable.
Strong stakeholder consultation, facilitation and practical training skills.
Fluent in English with excellent report-writing skills.
Interested consultants shall submit following documentation:
No conflict of interest arises while taking this assignment
Application, Cover Letter, and CV must be sent in English.
